description.narrative: Enhance the efficiency, safety and climate resilience of selected transport and logistics infrastructure corridors in Madagascar

This project intends to complement current road projects by financing climate-resilient upgrades or rehabilitation of selected priority multimodal transport and logistics infrastructure in line with Madagascar's 2024-2039 National Transport Plan. It aims to improve connectivity among major international and domestic transport corridors, to contribute to a more efficient business environment, lower transport costs, increase resilience, and enhance security and safety compliance at secondary airports. The project focuses on: (i) the Tananarive-Tamatave corridor through railway rehabilitation, the construction of a logistics platform near Antananarivo to manage heavy traffic entering the city, and improvements to infrastructure at Tamatave airport; (ii) the RN4 (National Road 4) and RN7 corridors via the rehabilitation of the ports of Majunga and Tulear, as well as Tulear airport; and (iii) the Pangalanes canal - RN12 corridor, with the rehabilitation of key sections of the canal and improvements to infrastructure at Fort-Dauphin airport. It also includes institutional capacity building for public transport entities, with attention to strengthening oversight and coordination and streamlining regulatory procedures to promote governance and competition across modes of transport. The project has 04 components. Component 1. Modernization and reform of railway transport. The project will finance the following activities that are grouped into five sub-components: Sub-component 1.1 - Rehabilitation and reinforcement of priority sections of Tananarive – Cote Est (TCE) and Tananarive-Antsirabe (TA) railway lines, Sub-component 1.2 - Construction of Dry Port and Terminal Facility, Sub-component 1.3 - Support to Madarail operations; Sub-component 1.4 - Preparatory studies to modernize the Fianarantsoa- Cote Est (FCE) railway line and to restore other railway lines, Sub-component 1.5 - Support to capacity-building and reform in rail transport. Component 2. Ports rehabilitation, waterways reopening of, and maritime and river transport reform. The component aims to rehabilitate the secondary ports of Tulear and Majunga to enhance their climate resilience and operational efficiency. It consists of five sub-components: Sub-component 2.1 - Rehabilitation of the port of Majunga; Sub-component 2.2 - Rehabilitation of the port of Tulear; Sub-component 2.3 - Rehabilitation of the Pangalanes canal; Sub-component 2.4 - Support to management and regulation of maritime and river operations; Sub-component 2.5- Construction/rehabilitation of tertiary/cabotage ports; Sub-component 2.6 - Support to the reform of APMF organization; Sub-component 2.7 - Capacity building and support to APMF for project implementation.Component 3. Rehabilitation and upgrade of regional airports and support to air transport sector including Sub-component 3.1 - Rehabilitation and modernization of Tamatave and Fort-Dauphin airports; Sub-component 3.2 - Rehabilitation and modernization of Tulear airport; Sub-component 3.3 - Support to Air Transport Sector reform and preparatory studies; Sub-component 3.4 - Capacity building and support to ADEMA project for implementation.Component 4. Support to project coordination and resettlement.
